instantiated_cells.justification: Section 1-e(a)(1) exempts from registration any lobbyist who does not expend, incur or receive in excess of $5,000 (for 2006 and after) in reportable compensation and expenses for lobbying, establishing the compensation/expense threshold for lobbyist registration.

Section 1-e(a)(1) sets the registration threshold based on combined "reportable compensation and expenses" exceeding $5,000, meaning expenditures by the lobbyist count toward the same $5,000 threshold triggering registration.

Section 1-h(b)(5)(ii) provides that expenses of $75 or less may be listed in the aggregate, while expenses of more than $75 must be itemized as to amount, recipient, and purpose, establishing $75 as the per-item itemization threshold.

Section 1-e(a)(1) exempts lobbyists from registration if they don't exceed $5,000 in reportable compensation and expenses, and §§1-h(a) and 1-j(a) similarly use $5,000 as the threshold for bi-monthly and semi-annual reporting obligations, creating a de minimis exemption from filing.

No provision in the Lobbying Act establishes a time-percentage exemption from filing based on the share of an individual's compensated time devoted to lobbying; thresholds are entirely dollar-based, so no such percentage exists.
